## Shared infrastructure — `@keenmate/web-components-devkit` (read before touching examples/build files)

This repo follows the Keenmate component standard: the BlissFramework rulebook
(`C:\Git\BlissFramework\guidelines\web-components\` — structure, naming, CSS,
theming, README, CEM, publish) plus the devkit (`../web-components`, published
as `@keenmate/web-components-devkit`), which owns the example-site kit, the
Vite/Playwright configs and the deploy files. Do not re-create or patch those
locally — every local fork is how they drifted apart.

- **Never add** `examples-chapter-nav.js`, `examples-copy-link.js`,
  `examples-controls-store.js`, `examples-shared.css`, `plausible-snippet.html`
  or `scripts/check-variable-manifest.mjs`. The chapter nav, copy-link buttons,
  shared styles, theme switch, version badge and analytics are injected into
  every root `*.html` page by the Vite plugin automatically.
- **Generated — do not edit:** `Dockerfile`, `nginx.conf`, `Makefile`,
  `.dockerignore` (they start with a `GENERATED by kmwc sync` header). Change
  `package.json#kmwc` and run `npx kmwc sync`, or fix the template in the devkit.
  Repo-specific make targets go in `Makefile.local`.
- **Per-component settings** (title, tagline, CSS prefix, ports, accent colours,
  analytics id, image name, canonical origin) live **only** in `package.json#kmwc`.
- **Example page styles:** shared rules are in `@layer kmwc` and read
  `--base-*` tokens (pages support light / dark / auto via the theme switch), so
  any unlayered rule wins. Put component-only rules in `examples-local.css`.
  Re-theme with `kmwc.theme.accentColor`, never by copying CSS. If a second
  component needs a pattern, it belongs in the devkit.
- **Example pages are fragments:** no `<html>`/`<head>`/`<header>` — start with
  `<meta name="kmwc:title" content="…">`, the devkit layout adds the rest. Shared text
  goes in `partials/` via `<kmwc-include>`; show code with `<kmwc-demo>` (the live
  markup IS the snippet) — never hand-copy a demo into a `.code-block`.
- **Controls persistence:**
  `import { attachControlsPersistence } from '@keenmate/web-components-devkit/examples'`.
  **Landing page:** `renderExamplesIndex({ pages })` from the same module.
- **Found a bug in a shared helper?** Fix it in `../web-components` (so every
  component gets it), not here. Say so in your summary if you can't.
- **Never ship AI-assistant files:** `package.json` `files` must keep
  `"!**/CLAUDE.md"` and `"!**/.claude"` (a `CLAUDE.md` you add under `src/` is
  otherwise published with it).
- Before finishing: `npx kmwc doctor` must pass — it runs the devkit checks,
  checks the `npm pack` file list for dev-only files, and runs the rulebook's
  `*.checks.sh` suites.

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Status

v1 is implemented (milestones M0–M8 of `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`). The plan remains the design
spec and records the intent behind the behaviour; `docs/usage.md` is the public API reference.

## Commands

A `Makefile` (generated by `kmwc sync`; repo targets in `Makefile.local`) wraps these (run `make`
for the list). It also has `make kill-port`, `make publish-dry`, `make publish-rc` (the `rc`
dist-tag) and `make publish` (`latest`), plus `make image-build` / `image-run` (examples site on
nginx, port 12410; see BUILD.md). Don't run the publish targets unless the user asks.

- `npm run dev` — Vite dev server on port **12400** (`index.html` hub + `examples-*.html`; ports come from `package.json#kmwc`)
- `npm run build` — `cem analyze` → Vite library build into `dist/` → `check:vars:strict`
- `npm run build:examples` / `preview:examples` — the static examples site in `dist-examples/` (served on 12401)
- `npm run test:unit` — vitest (happy-dom), specs in `test/unit/`. Single file: `npx vitest run test/unit/palette.test.ts`; by name: `npx vitest run -t "context search"`
- `npm run test:e2e` — Playwright against the dev server (reused if running); specs in `e2e/`, fixture page `test/fixture.html`. Single spec: `npx playwright test e2e/wizard.spec.ts`. `e2e/mobile.spec.ts` runs only in the `mobile` (Pixel 7) project
- `npm run check:vars` — `kmwc check-vars`: validate `component-variables.manifest.json` against the built bundle (the shadow CSS is inlined there), in `consumed` mode

## Architecture

`<web-command-palette>` is a framework-agnostic web component. It owns the whole command-palette
state machine and talks to hosts only through properties, events (`cp-*`) and async callbacks
(`searchCallback`, `stepOptionsCallback`). It replaces three drifting implementations (pure-admin
vanilla, svelte-pure-admin, keen-pure-admin LiveComponent). **Top design priority: easy to
configure** — `commands` + `searchCallback` must be a complete setup.

- `src/palette.ts` — `PaletteMachine`, DOM-free. Owns modes (`idle`, `command-list`,
  `command-step`, `context-list`, `context-search`, `global-search`), input routing, the wizard,
  filtering, debounced/abortable provider calls and client-side pagination. Exposes read-only
  view state (`items`, `activeIndex`, `listVersion`, `input`, `lockedLength`, …) and reports
  terminal outcomes through `host.effect()`. Unit-tested directly via `test/unit/helpers.ts`.
- `src/render.ts` — builds the shadow DOM once (`createShell`) and patches it (`Renderer`). Results
  are rebuilt only when `listVersion`/list state changes; moving the active row only toggles a
  class. Markup must match pure-admin-core's `snippets/command-palette.html`.
- `src/keyboard.ts` — the document-level `GlobalKeys` (Ctrl/⌘+K, `g <letter>`) and the input
  keydown map.
- `src/web-component.ts` — thin `BlissElement` subclass: the `static inputs` / `static events`
  tables (CEM metadata is generated from them), the `MachineHost` adapter, overlay/scroll-lock,
  presentation (phone fullscreen sheet), focus. Only the first connected instance owns the global keys.
- `src/usage.ts` — `UsageStore`: favorites + recents (frecency-ranked, pruned to 50 non-favorites),
  persisted via `localStorage` (`usage-key`) or the host's `loadUsageCallback`/`saveUsageCallback`.
  The machine records uses (instant commands, completed runs + answers, contexts, results) and
  offers a run's remembered answers when it's replayed (`#replay`; Enter = `commit()` fast-forwards,
  Tab = `select()` one step).
- `src/filter.ts`, `src/icons.ts`, `src/types.ts` — substring filtering, icon rendering, public types.

### Example pages

The pages use the devkit examples kit (see the block at the top). `index.html` calls
`renderExamplesIndex({ pages })` with the page registry. Each `examples-<feature>.html` is a
fragment: `kmwc:*` meta tags, then `.card` sections with numbered `<h2>`s (each one a chapter),
using only the kit's page classes — the theming gallery's `<style>` is the one exception, because
those rules are the example. Controls sit in `.controls` and are saved with
`attachControlsPersistence('<page-key>')`. Shared demo data is in `examples-data.js`.
`e2e/examples.spec.ts` checks the hub registry and every page.

### CSS pipeline (non-obvious)

`src/css/main.scss` `@use`s pure-admin-core's partials by relative path into `node_modules`
(never copied). `scripts/shadow-css.mjs` compiles it with plain Sass through a Vite plugin
(`shadowCssPlugin`) — Vite's own Sass importer can't be used because it applies package `exports`
to bare `@import`s inside core. The PostCSS step then (1) injects core's theme defaults as
`var()` **fallbacks** rather than declarations, so a host theme on `:root` is never shadowed, and
(2) rewrites `Nrem` → `calc(N * var(--base-rem, 10px))` because pure-admin assumes a 10px root.
It also (3) maps scale font sizes to `--base-font-size-*`, and (4) enforces the component's own
namespace: core's `--pa-command-palette-*` / `--pa-icon-*` become `--cp-*` (`--_cp-*` = private),
every other `--pc-*` / `--pa-*` read is replaced by its `--base-*` fallback, and the navbar
search-pill rules are dropped. **The shipped CSS reads only `--cp-*` and `--base-*`** — never add
a `--pa-*` / `--pc-*` read in `src/css`; icons are `--cp-icon-*` → `--base-icon-*` → inline SVG.
The plugin fails the build if a `--pa-*` / `--pc-*` variable survives, and `kmwc check-vars`
reads the built bundle.

## Invariants that are easy to break

See plan §10. These are the bugs that motivated the project.

- Static vs. dynamic: the `/` and `:` lists and non-`search` steps filter client-side. Only global
  search, context search and `search: true` steps call providers, debounced (`searchDebounce`).
- A context search with an empty query must NOT call `searchCallback`; show `labels.typeToSearch`.
  The input keeps a locked `"<shortcut> "` prefix.
- Global search prepends matching commands/contexts (works with no `searchCallback`), then appends
  provider results.
- Keyboard navigation never awaits a provider and must not bump `listVersion`.
- Superseded requests are aborted via `AbortSignal`, and late results are dropped.
- Callback arguments and event details must stay plain JSON, because the LiveView bridge
  serializes them. `searchCallback`/`stepOptionsCallback` are read live. `data-search-event` /
  `data-step-options-event` are reserved for the future `../keen-web-commandpalette` bridge.
- The component closes itself after `cp-select` / `cp-complete` / `cp-command`, and the host
  performs the effect. Commands first collapse to the one-line confirmation (`#showConfirmation` in the
  element, `.cp-confirming` hides everything but `.cp-confirm`; the event still fires immediately, `cp-close` follows) — while `#confirmTimer` is set,
  `#render()` must not repaint over it. Instant commands fire only `cp-command`. A `// FUTURE:` note in
  `#onEffect` marks where keep-open/directives would go.
- RTL comes from inherited `direction`: CSS must stay logical (`inset-inline-*`, `margin-inline-*`,
  `inline-size` — no physical left/right), rendered text runs are wrapped in `<bdi>`, and ←/→
  paging swaps via `this.isRTL` (read per keydown, so runtime `dir` flips need no rebuild).
- Icons and strings are data. There is no built-in icon set, and every visible string comes from `labels`.
- Usage entries must stay plain JSON (they're persisted). A run's branch steps are NOT stored: on
  replay, a forking answer is resolved against the step's current options, and Enter's
  fast-forward stops at a step whose list isn't loaded yet rather than guess the branch.
- `Step.load`, `Context.search` and `Step.shouldShow` are JS-only conveniences; the central
  `stepOptionsCallback` / `searchCallback` must keep working for server-driven hosts.

Out of scope here: the keen bridge, Svelte/React/Razor wrappers, the directive-return channel, and migrating the existing palettes.
